In the former event we were in the "A" section of the race with such clubs as Poly H., Achilles, Walton, Herne Hill, and Southgate H., and our team of Jack Brown, Holtum, Sexton, and Badiali did well to gain third place.

Bob Taylor won the 1 mile in 4 min. 28.5 secs., while Holtum and Basil Walden were first two home in the 100 yards. Ian Badiali won the 880 yards in fine style, beating Allen of Ealing H., the Middlesex champion, with Jack Brown and Ray Tooby also behind him.

"Ginger" Holtum was 2nd in the Middlesex Senior 100 yards championship, and Bob Taylor ran well to finish 2nd in the 880 yards. Basil Walden and Ginger Holtum both qualified for the final of the 100 yards, which Basil won with Holtum in 3rd place. Ray Tooby and Bob Taylor also qualified for the 880 yards final and Bob ran a fine race to finish in 2nd place, but Ray was almost run-out and could only struggle in for 6th position.

In the Senior events we saw Holtum win the 100 yards, and he was also 2nd in the 220, while Bill Lucas won the 1 mile in 4 min. 36.3 secs., and John Bromley, making a return after an operation for appendicitis, was 2nd to Peter Pirie in the 2 miles.

Bob Taylor won the 880 yards while Holtum was second in the 100 yards, and Vern Blowfield won the 3 miles run in 15 min. 4 secs. Ian Badiali was second in the 440 but we were short of competitors for the two field events which were included in the match.

This evening match on the village green saw a large crowd of spectators, and as we won both the senior and junior matches, they must have been duly impressed by our lads' performances. Basil Walden won the senior 100 yds. with Holtum in second place, and J.

Unfortunately, owing to holidays, etc., we were minus the services of Walden and Holtum, and as both Sexton and Bartlett were required for the 4 x 440, it was decided not to field a team for the sprint relay.

Dicky Bartlett ran 3rd in the 220 yds., which was won by Brian Shenton, and then came the sensation of the meeting, McDonald Bailey could only finish 3rd in the 100 yds. and was beaten by Ruddy of A.P.M., and our own Ron Holtum in 10.1 secs.

Basil Walden qualified for the final of the 100 yds., and was 5th, with Holtum unplaced in his heat. Walden and Banstead both failed to get through their heats in the 220 yds., and we missed Denis Merrett in this event.
Our team of Holtum, Marshall, Walden and Mayers were drawn on the outside and with Marshall being short of training we could only finish in 6th place.
Held at the White City on July 10th-11th, and on the Friday we saw the heats of the 100 yards, and we had Holtum, Mayers and Walden competing, but without success.
In the South Western Area Championships held at Tooting Bec on 17th July all four finalists in the 100 yards were Belgrave members and the finishing order was R. Holtum, R.

Denis was also 2nd in the 100 yards and our other sprinters Mayers, Walden and Holtum all ran well in their heats of 100 and 220 yards. Ted Gaworski took 2nd place in the Shot put with a personal best and Mal Ash was 2nd in the High Jump and 5th in the hurdles.
A new holder was also produced in the Senior 100 yards, the finalists being Mayers, Walden, Butler, Merrett, Key and Holtum., Merrett eventually winning from Mayers with Walden third.
The first track event was the heats of the 100 yards in which both Holtum and Mayers qualified for the final, won later by Ivan with Ron third.

The highlights of this year's Championships, held on 15th and 16th July, as far as Belgrave was concerned. was the excellent running of Ron Holtum to be the first Belgrave Harrier to reach the final of the 100 yards, for as long as most of us can remember, and Dennis Merrett's third place in the 220 yards Hurdles.
The 4 x 110 team of Merritt, Holtum, Jones and Mayers won their heat in 43.3secs., the fastest of the two, which looked as though we had a very good chance in the final.
We were weakened again in the senior events, Ron Holtum having the flu and Jack Brown unable to be present. Bob Taylor tried to contact Charlie Walker but failed.
